content.title: About
content.content: Potato tots are small fried balls made from grated potato, breadcrumbs and seasonings. They are popular as a snack in schools and cafeterias, and also as a quick home snack.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Potato tots were first introduced in the United States in the 1950s as a convenient way to use leftover potatoes.
In Russia they are often called “potato croquettes” or “potato balls”.
For a crunchy crust, tots are frequently rolled in cornflakes or breadcrumbs before frying.
Most school‑supply batches are produced from frozen semi‑finished pieces that are flash‑frozen after shaping.
The name “tots” comes from “tater tots”, where “tater” is a colloquial term for potato.

items.title: Source of potassium
items.content: Potatoes are rich in potassium, which supports normal heart and muscle function.

items.title: Vitamin C
items.content: A small amount of vitamin C survives quick frying, providing antioxidant protection.

items.title: Energy supply
items.content: Potato tots deliver fast‑acting carbohydrates, useful for growing children and active students.

items.title: Contains fiber
items.content: Grated potato retains some dietary fiber, aiding digestion.

items.title: Versatile pairing
items.content: Tots can be served with vegetable dips, increasing overall vitamin intake.

items.title: High fat content
items.content: Frying adds significant oil, so portion control is recommended.

items.title: Salt
items.content: Salted versions may exceed daily sodium limits, especially for children.

items.title: Allergy to breadcrumbs
items.content: Some recipes use wheat breadcrumbs, which can be problematic for people with celiac disease.

items.title: Choking hazard for young children
items.content: Small tots can become lodged in the airway of toddlers.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Potato tots can be served hot as a standalone snack, with ketchup, sour cream, or vegetable sauce. They reheat well in the oven or microwave. In schools they are often included in lunch menus alongside vegetable sticks.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep frozen tots in a freezer at –18 °C. After thawing, cook immediately and do not leave at room temperature for more than 2 hours.
